stories.title: Exercise lifts mood and quality of life in IBD, but a new meta-analysis finds no clear drop in inflammation markers
stories.summary: <cite index="38-1">A September 2026 meta-analysis and systematic review (in Chinese) found exercise may improve mental health and quality of life in people with IBD. It did not significantly change CRP or faecal calprotectin. For calprotectin the weighted mean difference was 18.59 with a 95% CI of -25.44 to 62.61 (P=0.41).</cite> <cite index="38-1">The authors say the wide confidence intervals mean an effect on inflammation can't be ruled out. They add that larger RCTs and further confirmation of safety are still needed.</cite> The takeaway is that the gym is good for how you feel and function, but it is not a substitute for anti-inflammatory treatment.
stories.whyItMatters: Train for strength, fitness and mood, but don't treat the gym as a replacement for your IBD medicine. Keep checking calprotectin and CRP with your care team, and tell them if your training load changes.
stories.source: Medical Health and Clinical Practice (via ResearchGate)

stories.title: IBD drug pipeline: biosimilar ustekinumab now at anti-TNF prices, vedolizumab copy expected by late 2027
stories.summary: <cite index="55-6">Biosimilar ustekinumab is already available at anti-TNF prices.</cite> <cite index="55-7">A biosimilar vedolizumab looks likely by the end of 2027.</cite> <cite index="55-13">Generic tofacitinib was approved in the UK this year.</cite> The source is an expert's Substack analysis rather than a regulator, and the dates are projections.
stories.whyItMatters: If your clinic proposes a switch to a biosimilar or generic, ask how switching will be monitored and what happens if it doesn't work for you. Ask whether your regular drug has a cheaper copy coming.

stories.title: PANCCO updates Latin American ulcerative colitis treatment guideline with newer biologics and small molecules
stories.summary: The Pan American Crohn's and Colitis Organisation (PANCCO) published its third update of treatment recommendations for moderate-to-severe UC in adults. The update adds newer biologics and small-molecule drugs, using rapid GRADE guideline methods. It says treatment choice should be individualised by prior therapy, comorbidities, cardiovascular and thrombotic risk, local availability and patient preference. The abstract I could access gave no per-drug numbers.
stories.whyItMatters: Ask your gastroenterologist how your own cardiovascular and clot risk, including smoking and vaping, affects which advanced therapy suits you. Also ask which options are actually available through your national health system or insurer.
stories.source: Revista de Gastroenterología del Perú (PANCCO guideline)

stories.title: THC cannabis for IBD: systematic review finds no clear benefit on remission or endoscopy
stories.summary: <cite index="3-11">Remission (3 trials, n=150), endoscopic scores (2 trials, n=88), quality of life and nausea consistently did not differ meaningfully between THC cannabis and control.</cite> The authors also note that <cite index="2-3">unblinding and poor exposure measurement lowered the quality of the evidence.</cite> A separate 2026 patient survey found <cite index="1-7">59.3% of respondents believed marijuana had reduced their opioid use</cite>, but that is perception, not proof.
stories.whyItMatters: Cannabis may feel like it helps symptoms, but trials show no measurable effect on gut inflammation. Tell your IBD team if you use it, so they can weigh it against your symptoms and any other medicines.

stories.title: Brazil's ANVISA registers a ustekinumab biosimilar (Yesintek) for Crohn's and ulcerative colitis
stories.summary: On 11 May 2026 ANVISA published the registration of Yesintek, a ustekinumab biosimilar assessed by the comparability pathway against Stelara. It is indicated for adults with moderate-to-severe active Crohn's disease or UC after inadequate response, loss of response or intolerance to conventional or biologic therapy. It is also indicated for psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. The agency's notice gives no price or launch date.
stories.whyItMatters: Biosimilars can widen access and may lower costs, but only your team can say if a switch makes sense. Ask whether it applies to you and whether the SUS or your insurer covers it.

stories.title: Stem-cell therapy darvadstrocel fails phase 3 trial for Crohn's perianal fistulas
stories.summary: <cite index="29-5">The ADMIRE CD II trial enrolled 568 adults with Crohn's and complex perianal fistulas in Europe, Israel and North America.</cite> <cite index="29-9">At 24 weeks, combined remission was 48.8% with darvadstrocel versus 46.3% with placebo, which was not statistically significant.</cite> The high placebo rate suggests that the surgical preparation itself did much of the work.
stories.whyItMatters: If you have perianal fistulas, ask your team which options still have solid evidence behind them, such as surgical preparation, biologics and seton drainage. Also ask about trials you could join.
stories.source: GI & Hepatology News (AGA), reporting a Gastroenterology paper

stories.title: Low muscle mass in Crohn's disease signals a rougher disease course
stories.summary: <cite index="13-4,13-5">A retrospective study of 52 Crohn's patients, published in August 2026, found that sarcopenia (low skeletal muscle index) was an independent predictor of an unfavourable outcome. So were faecal calprotectin above 129 μg/g and complicated disease behaviour.</cite> It is a small, single-cohort observational study, so it shows an association rather than proof that muscle loss causes worse disease. It does suggest that muscle loss deserves attention alongside inflammation.
stories.region: Not stated in the excerpt (MDPI journal)
stories.whyItMatters: If you are losing muscle or strength despite training, mention it to your gastroenterologist and ask about a dietitian review. It can be an early warning sign, not just a gym problem.

stories.title: Half of Crohn's patients on infliximab had weak grip strength, even without formal sarcopenia
stories.summary: <cite index="16-4">A cross-sectional study of 84 Crohn's patients on infliximab (76.2% male, mean age 35) measured muscle function.</cite> <cite index="15-9">Half of the cohort had muscle strength below age- and sex-adjusted norms, yet none met the criteria for confirmed sarcopenia.</cite> Muscle scans or body-composition numbers can therefore look fine while strength is already reduced.
stories.region: Single tertiary centre (country not stated in the excerpt)
stories.whyItMatters: Strength tests such as grip strength can pick up problems that weight and scans miss, so track your lifts or ask for a simple grip test at a clinic visit. Resistance training with dietitian input is the usual response to low strength.

stories.title: PROFILE 5-year results (top-down vs step-up in Crohn's) previewed as UEG Week top abstract
stories.summary: A clinician's preview of the only IBD top abstract at UEG Week 2026 gives the five-year PROFILE figures. Crohn's surgery was needed in 13% of the step-up group vs 3% of the top-down infliximab group (adjusted hazard ratio 5.2). Admissions fell from 21% to 11%, and progression to stricturing or penetrating disease fell from 17% to 7%. The formal presentation is scheduled for 19 October. These figures come from a preview blog, not the presented abstract.
stories.whyItMatters: It adds long-term randomised evidence on whether starting an advanced therapy at diagnosis changes the chance of surgery. Treatment timing is a decision for each person and their care team.

stories.title: PROFILE 5-year results: early top-down infliximab cut the need for Crohn's surgery (UEG Week preview)
stories.summary: A commentary previewing UEG Week 2026 describes the five-year PROFILE results, now published in full. 13% of people randomised to step-up treatment had needed Crohn's-related abdominal surgery, against 3% with top-down infliximab from diagnosis (adjusted hazard ratio 5.2). Treating about nine people top-down would prevent one operation. The trial is a Top Abstract at UEG Week on Monday 19 October. This summary relies on the commentator's description, not on the paper itself.
stories.whyItMatters: It adds long-term randomised evidence to the debate about starting a biologic early in Crohn's, which is a decision for patient and clinician. Surgery rates are only one outcome, and the trial compares treatment strategies, not individual drugs.
stories.source: Atomic IBD (Charlie Lees) – UEG Week 2026 preview

stories.title: Mirikizumab one-year composite outcomes: corticosteroid-free deep remission in Crohn's and comprehensive disease control in UC
stories.summary: Lilly's new post hoc analyses of its phase 3 trials found that 20.4% of Crohn's patients in VIVID-1 reached corticosteroid-free deep remission at one year. This composite required clinical remission, endoscopic remission and no steroid use. Similar multi-goal outcomes were seen in UC, including in patients who had failed a prior biologic (over a third of the UC group and nearly half of the Crohn's group). The data are company-run post hoc analyses, shown at ACG 2026 and due at UEG Week 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: Composite targets that combine symptoms, endoscopy and steroid-free status show what a stricter treat-to-target goal looks like. Only about one in five Crohn's patients met it, and the analysis comes from the manufacturer, so it is a company's view of the data.
stories.source: Eli Lilly press release (ACG 2026 / UEG Week 2026)

stories.title: Review: drug options for IBD fatigue within a whole-person approach
stories.summary: A narrative review published 15 October 2026 looks at why fatigue happens in IBD. It covers drugs aimed at fatigue itself and at contributors such as anaemia, psychiatric conditions, sleep problems and pain. It places drug treatment inside a multidisciplinary plan that also includes non-drug approaches. It is a review, not a new trial, so it gives no new efficacy numbers.
stories.whyItMatters: Fatigue is a common and disabling problem in IBD, and this review gives people and their care teams a framework for discussing its several possible causes. It does not show that any specific drug works.

stories.title: Mirikizumab post-hoc data at UEG Week: 'comprehensive disease control' in UC and deep remission in Crohn's at one year
stories.summary: In a post-hoc analysis of the LUCENT-2 trial, 27.7% of people with ulcerative colitis on mirikizumab (Omvoh) met a strict composite at week 52. The composite combined clinical remission, no steroids, histologic remission and calprotectin of 250 µg/g or lower. Reports give different placebo figures (9.4% vs 14%). In VIVID-1 in Crohn's, 20.4% reached steroid-free deep remission vs 2% on placebo. These are manufacturer-run post-hoc analyses, not new randomised trials.
stories.whyItMatters: The strict composite targets, which include histology and calprotectin, show how stringent 'remission' is becoming. They also show that fewer people reach these deeper targets than reach symptom remission.
stories.source: Lilly press release (UEG Week 2026), via BiotechReality and GuruFocus

stories.title: Subcutaneous risankizumab induction in Crohn's: 36% endoscopic remission at 24 weeks in phase 3 AFFIRM
stories.summary: At ACG 2026, AbbVie reported that 35.8% of people given risankizumab under the skin had endoscopic remission at week 24, against 9.1% on placebo. 36.6% of those with ulcers at baseline became ulcer-free. In patients new to advanced therapy, 45.1% reached endoscopic remission. Week-12 results had already met the co-primary endpoints, and the company has filed with the US FDA for an SC induction regimen. This is a company press release.
stories.whyItMatters: If approved, it could offer an under-the-skin alternative to the intravenous start-up doses now used for this drug. Results come from the company, and the regulatory decision is still pending.
stories.source: AbbVie press release (ACG 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting)

stories.title: Mucosal healing and normal calprotectin don't guarantee recovered quality of life in IBD
stories.summary: A Medscape article from 9 October 2026 says that mucosal healing and normal fecal calprotectin do not guarantee full recovery of quality of life. Some patients with controlled endoscopy and lab markers still have chronic fatigue, abdominal pain, anxiety and severe sleep disturbance. The snippet I could read does not give study numbers.
stories.whyItMatters: Symptoms such as fatigue, pain, anxiety and poor sleep can persist even when tests look good, so they may be worth raising with a care team in their own right.

stories.title: Subcutaneous infliximab beats IV in ileal Crohn's in pooled propensity-matched analysis (ACG 2026 late-breaker)
stories.summary: In a pooled, propensity-matched analysis, 65.7% of patients with ileal Crohn's disease on subcutaneous infliximab had an endoscopic response at week 54, versus 27.1% on IV infliximab. A separate LIBERTY post hoc analysis found that prior anti-drug antibodies did not blunt results when SC infliximab was restarted after a treatment break. Both analyses were sponsored by Celltrion and are not head-to-head randomized comparisons.
stories.whyItMatters: This suggests the SC form may work particularly well for ileal disease and may remain usable after a drug holiday. Because the comparison is matched rather than randomized and company-run, it is hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing.

stories.title: Meta-analysis: low BMI and prior GI surgery are linked to sarcopenia in IBD
stories.summary: A systematic review of 13 cohort studies covered 5,559 people with IBD, and 632 met criteria for low muscle mass or sarcopenia. Low BMI (OR 4.70) and a history of gastrointestinal surgery (OR 2.07) were associated with sarcopenia, both on low-certainty evidence. Biologic use, perianal disease and steroid use were linked to low muscle mass, mostly on very low-certainty evidence.
stories.whyItMatters: If you have IBD and are thin, you are in the group most likely to have low muscle. Ask your care team about checking grip strength or body composition, not just weight. These are observational associations and do not show that any treatment causes muscle loss.

stories.title: Re-analysis finds weekly training volume, not how it is split across sessions, tracks muscle growth
stories.summary: This preprint re-analysed the dataset behind a 2026 dose-response meta-regression. It used 220 effects from 35 randomized trials with 963 participants. At a fixed frequency, more weekly volume was linked to more hypertrophy (b = 0.170, 95% CI 0.076 to 0.263). In mostly male samples training each muscle 1 to 4 times a week, splitting that volume into more sessions made no detectable difference. A separate October 2026 medRxiv meta-analysis of volume-equated trials is also on the question. I could only see its introduction, not its results. Neither preprint has been peer reviewed.
stories.whyItMatters: If you are a hard gainer, put your effort into getting enough hard weekly sets per muscle. Then pick the number of sessions that fits your schedule and recovery.

stories.title: Anvisa authorizes a creatine strength claim for resistance-trained adults over 55
stories.summary: Brazil's health regulator published Normative Instruction 470/2026 after its board met on 16 September 2026. It allows a claim that daily creatine plus regular resistance training can increase the strength gains from training in adults over 55. The claim only applies to products that meet the minimum and maximum creatine amounts set in the existing supplement rules.
stories.whyItMatters: Brazil now formally recognises creatine combined with resistance training as having evidence for strength gains, but only in older adults. Younger hard gainers should buy only registered products and check the batch notices, since several creatine lots were recalled this year.
stories.source: BHB Food (trade news on Anvisa IN 470/2026)

stories.title: Creatine for 12 weeks added lean tissue and strength in middle-aged adults, even without a training program
stories.summary: A Texas A&M-led 12-week trial in middle-aged and older adults found creatine helped people gain muscle and strength without a structured workout program. Adding exercise and a calorie-reduced diet produced bigger strength gains, more lean tissue and fat loss. The published paper is labelled a randomized controlled trial, but the participants were not underweight and the diet arm involved calorie restriction, not a surplus.
stories.whyItMatters: Creatine is still the best-supported add-on for lean mass. These results come from middle-aged adults who were not underweight, so a hard gainer should not expect muscle gain without training. Lean-mass gains on body scans can also include water stored in muscle.
stories.source: Texas A&M University via ScienceDaily (paper: J Int Soc Sports Nutr, Aug 2026)

stories.title: Large meta-regression: volume drives muscle growth with diminishing returns; frequency matters more for strength
stories.summary: This Sports Medicine meta-regression pooled 67 studies with 2,058 participants (79% male, average age about 25). Weekly set volume and frequency each had their own dose-response relationship with hypertrophy and strength, and the curve for strength flattened more steeply. Frequency's effect on hypertrophy was compatible with a negligible effect, while strength gains rose with frequency, with diminishing returns. The authors also stress counting direct and indirect sets separately.
stories.whyItMatters: Extra sets help muscle growth, but with diminishing returns, so aim for steady progressive training of each muscle rather than maximal volume. Training a muscle more often mainly helps strength.

stories.title: Anvisa recalls and suspends creatine and other supplement lots over quality and labeling failures
stories.summary: On 19 June 2026 Anvisa suspended 11 lots of IDNLABS supplements, including creatine powder, BCAA, beta-alanine and multivitamins. Press reports cite ingredient amounts below the label, use outside legal limits and unauthorized claims. On 25 June it also seized an unknown-origin capsule supplement (Artro100) and suspended three lots of IDNLABS creatine gummies because the creatine content was outside the permitted limits.
stories.whyItMatters: Even ordinary creatine and amino-acid products can fail quality checks. Hard gainers on a tight budget should check Anvisa notices and batch numbers, and avoid products of unknown origin or with therapeutic claims.

stories.title: UNSW trial: 5 g/day creatine gave no extra lean mass during resistance training
stories.summary: A controlled trial from the University of New South Wales, published in Nutrients, found no significant difference in muscle gain between people taking creatine and those who did not. The senior author said 5 g of creatine a day made no difference to lean mass gained during resistance training. This is a null result at the commonly recommended maintenance dose.
stories.whyItMatters: Creatine does not always add measurable muscle on top of consistent lifting. Training, protein and total calories matter most, and creatine is a small optional extra. A separate 2026 meta-analysis reported by News-Medical found lean-mass benefits only when creatine was paired with resistance training.
stories.source: Technology Networks (reporting a study in Nutrients, UNSW)

stories.title: More is not always better: over 60 weekly sets gave no extra growth in trained male athletes
stories.summary: A study in trained male athletes found that raising resistance training volume beyond 60 sets per week gave no statistically significant extra gains in muscle size or strength. The higher volume also did not turn non-responders into responders. The authors suggest the best volume for hypertrophy may be below 58 sets per week.
stories.whyItMatters: Very high volume is not a shortcut for people who struggle to grow. Moderate volume you can recover from, together with enough food, is a more realistic plan.

stories.title: Oral icotrokinra pill beat placebo for response in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis
stories.summary: In a phase 2b randomized trial of 252 adults with moderately to severely active UC, clinical response at week 12 was 63%, 58% and 55% with 400, 200 and 100 mg daily icotrokinra, versus 27% with placebo. At 400 mg, clinical remission was 30% vs 11% and endoscopic improvement was 37% vs 14%. Adverse events were similar across groups through week 28 (60-66%).
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests a once-daily pill that blocks the interleukin-23 pathway could one day be an alternative to injected or infused IL-23 antibodies, though larger and longer trials are needed.
stories.source: The New England journal of medicine
stories.originalTitle: Phase 2 Trial of Icotrokinra for Patients with Ulcerative Colitis

stories.title: Etrasimod lowers inflammatory immune cells in blood and gut lining in UC
stories.summary: Using blood from 782 and gut biopsies from 611 patients in the phase 3 ELEVATE UC trials, etrasimod reduced circulating T- and B-cell subsets at week 12 compared with placebo. Gut tissue showed fewer T cells, B cells, myeloid cells and neutrophils, with reduced IL-17 and IL-8 signaling. Changes consistent with tissue repair were most prominent in patients who reached remission.
stories.whyItMatters: It helps explain how this oral UC medication works on the immune system and the gut lining.
stories.originalTitle: Etrasimod reduces circulating and mucosal inflammatory lymphocyte populations and alters innate immune and non-immune cell signatures in intestinal mucosa: ELEVATE UC phase 3 clinical data

stories.title: Fast-recovery surgery pathways shorten hospital stays for people with IBD
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 18 studies (one randomized trial, 17 observational) found enhanced recovery protocols cut hospital stay by about 1.6 days (moderate certainty). There were no clear differences in 30-day readmissions, reoperations or complications, though certainty for these was low to very low.
stories.whyItMatters: If you need bowel surgery, enhanced recovery programs may mean a shorter hospital stay without evidence of more readmissions or complications, though the evidence is mostly observational.
stories.source: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
stories.originalTitle: Enhanced recovery after colorectal surgery in patients with inflammatory bowel disease to reduce hospital length of stay: A systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Stem cell therapy closed about 6 in 10 Crohn's perianal fistulas long-term
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 18 studies with 750 patients and 12 months to 4 years of follow-up found a pooled long-term healing rate of 59% in randomized trials and 63% across all designs. No treatment-related deaths or clear therapy-linked cancers were found.
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests stem cell treatment may give lasting healing for fistulas that haven't responded to standard care, although study designs differ.
stories.source: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
stories.originalTitle: Long-term clinical outcomes of stem cell-based interventions in Crohn's-related perianal fistula: A systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Under-the-skin infliximab kept most children with IBD in remission after switching
stories.summary: A pooled analysis of five cohorts (162 children, mostly Crohn's) found treatment persistence of about 90% and clinical remission of about 90% at roughly 6 months. Infliximab blood levels roughly doubled after the switch, new antidrug antibodies were rare (0.7%), and injection site reactions occurred in 11%. Certainty was low to very low, and nearly all children switched while already in remission.
stories.whyItMatters: It offers early reassurance for families considering a switch from intravenous to subcutaneous infliximab, which is currently off-label in children, but it does not show the injection can start treatment.
stories.originalTitle: Subcutaneous infliximab for maintenance therapy in children and adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Trial testing a phone-based CBT program for fatigue in IBD remission is under way
stories.summary: This is a protocol for an open-label, waitlist-controlled randomized trial of a 7-week app-based cognitive behavioral program for fatigue in people with IBD in remission. 351 patients were randomized; 151 of 502 screened were excluded for having little fatigue (FACIT-F of 40 or higher). No results are available yet and are expected in 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: Fatigue is common even in remission, and this trial could show whether a scalable app-based approach helps, but there are no findings yet.
stories.originalTitle: Evaluation of a Mental Health Care App-Based Fatigue Management Program for Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Remission: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial

stories.title: COVID-19 didn't worsen IBD course, but interrupted biologics raised flare risk
stories.summary: Across four matched cohorts (about 1,300 patients), prior COVID-19 was not linked to worse IBD course (OR 1.06; 95% CI 0.76-1.49). COVID-19 was linked to delayed or stopped biologics (OR 10.44), and flares were more frequent when biologics were delayed or stopped (about 52% vs 18%).
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests the bigger concern after COVID-19 may be interrupted IBD treatment rather than the infection itself, though the evidence is limited to a few observational cohorts.
stories.originalTitle: COVID-19 AND IBD: LOOK BEYOND THE VIRUS. A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS FOCUSED ON BIOLOGIC THERAPY CONTINUITY

stories.title: Neutrophil traps are high in IBD and blocking them eased colitis in animal models
stories.summary: A review of 48 studies found markers of neutrophil extracellular traps were raised in the gut and blood of people with IBD and linked to more severe disease and poorer prognosis. In animal models, blocking or breaking down these traps reduced disease activity and tissue damage and improved gut barrier function. Several results were not robust in sensitivity analyses.
stories.whyItMatters: This is early-stage science pointing to a possible future treatment target, with no human treatment trials yet.
stories.originalTitle: Neutrophil extracellular traps as a potential therapeutic target in inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis

stories.title: Stem cells and anti-TNF drugs both help Crohn's fistulas; no clear winner
stories.summary: A network meta-analysis of 15 randomized trials (2,475 patients) found stem cells improved fistula remission (OR 5.33) and response (OR 4.76) versus placebo. Anti-TNF drugs also improved fistula remission (OR 2.19) and were better for overall clinical remission (OR 2.41). Indirect comparison showed a non-significant trend favoring stem cells for fistula healing, and both had safety similar to placebo.
stories.whyItMatters: Both options appear to work for perianal Crohn's fistulas, but without head-to-head trials it is unclear which is better.
stories.originalTitle: Efficacy and safety of tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitors and mesenchymal stem cells in the treatment of fistulizing Crohn's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis

stories.title: Balloon dilation of Crohn's strictures helped avoid surgery over 7 years better than stents
stories.summary: In a long-term follow-up of 80 patients from the ProtDilat trial (median 77 months), 31.5% needed surgery. Balloon dilatation (HR 0.26), a single endoscopic treatment (HR 0.33) and no medical therapy intensification (HR 0.22) were linked to lower surgery risk. Adverse events were less frequent with endoscopic treatment than surgery (8.75% vs 36%).
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests endoscopic balloon dilation can delay or avoid surgery for many people with Crohn's strictures, though this is a retrospective follow-up of an open-label trial.
stories.originalTitle: Self-expandable metal stents versus endoscopic balloon dilatation for the treatment of strictures in Crohn's disease: a retrospective long-term follow-up of the ProtDilat study, an open label, multicenter, randomized trial
